hook: Andrew Zisserman completed Part III of the Mathematical Tripos at Cambridge and a PhD in theoretical physics at Sunderland Polytechnic before moving into computer vision. He began vision research at the University of Edinburgh in 1984, and in 1987 joined Mike Brady's robotics group at the University of Oxford, where he worked on multiple view geometry and later founded the Visual Geometry Group. With Karen Simonyan he co-authored Very Deep Convolutional Networks for Large-Scale Image Recognition in 2014, introducing the VGGNet architecture that became a benchmark for deep convolutional networks in image recognition. He has been affiliated with Google DeepMind as a researcher since 2014, including work on the Flamingo visual language model, while continuing as a Royal Society Research Professor at Oxford.

quick_facts: Born in 1957 in the United Kingdom
Holds a PhD in theoretical physics from Sunderland Polytechnic
Co-created VGGNet with Karen Simonyan in 2014, a landmark deep convolutional network for image recognition
Is the only person to have won the Marr Prize three times, in 1993, 1998, and 2003
Elected Fellow of the Royal Society in 2007 and received the Royal Society Milner Award in 2017
Has been affiliated with Google DeepMind as a researcher since 2014

achievements.title: VGGNet
achievements.impact: Co-created a deep convolutional network architecture that set a new standard for image classification and became a widely used backbone for later computer vision systems.

achievements.title: Multiple view geometry research
achievements.impact: Co-authored foundational work, including the book Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision, that shaped how 3D structure is recovered from images.

achievements.title: Visual Geometry Group leadership
achievements.impact: Built Oxford's Visual Geometry Group into one of the most influential computer vision research groups, training many researchers who went on to shape the field.

achievements.title: Flamingo visual language model
achievements.impact: Contributed to a DeepMind few-shot visual language model that helped establish techniques for combining vision and language understanding.
